title: When Is Imaging Actually Needed? Ottawa, Canadian C-spine and Back Pain Rules

hook.en: Too many scans cost money, worry patients and expose them to radiation; too few can miss a fracture. Learn the decision rules that tell you when to refer for an X-ray and when imaging will not help.
hook.ur: Bohat zyada scans paisa kharch karte hain, mareezon ko pareshan karte hain aur radiation dete hain; bohat kam fracture miss kar sakte hain. Woh decision rules seekhein jo batate hain X-ray ke liye refer kab karna hai aur imaging kab madad nahi karegi.

goal.en: By the end, you'll apply the Ottawa ankle and knee rules, the Canadian C-spine rule and the low back pain imaging guidance, explain why most back pain needs no scan and know which red flags mean image or refer straight away.
goal.ur: End tak aap Ottawa ankle aur knee rules, Canadian C-spine rule aur kamar dard ki imaging guidance istemal karenge, samjhayenge ke zyada tar kamar dard ko scan nahi chahiye aur jaanenge ke kaun si red flags ka matlab hai foran imaging ya refer.

text.en: A **clinical decision rule** is a short checklist, built from large studies, that tells you **which patients need an X-ray**. The best rules are **very sensitive** (they rarely miss a fracture), so a negative result lets you **safely skip the film**. They apply to the **people they were designed for** (for example alert adults with an acute injury) and do not replace judgement. For **low back pain**, guidelines advise **no routine imaging** unless there are **red flags or a progressive deficit**, because images often show harmless changes.
text.ur: **Clinical decision rule** chhoti checklist hai, bari studies se bani, jo batati hai **kin mareezon ko X-ray chahiye**. Behtareen rules **bohat sensitive** hote hain (fracture shayad hi miss karte hain), is liye negative nateeje par aap **film mehfooz taur par chhor sakte hain**. Yeh un **logon par lagti hain jin ke liye bani** (maslan hoshiyar bale jinhein taaza chot ho) aur faisla badalti nahi. **Kamar dard** ke liye guidelines **routine imaging nahi** kehti jab tak **red flags ya barhta nuqsan** na ho, kyunke tasveerein aksar begarar tabdeeliyan dikhati hain.

text.en: Think of a decision rule as **an airport security scanner**. It is set to be very sensitive, so it rarely lets a danger through, and most travellers who pass are safe. It will also stop some harmless people, which is acceptable. You do not search every bag by hand (every patient gets an X-ray) and you do not skip the scanner (guess), you use the scanner.
text.ur: Decision rule ko **airport ka security scanner** samjhein. Woh bohat sensitive rakha jata hai, is liye khatra shayad hi guzarta hai, aur zyada tar guzarne wale musafir mehfooz hote hain. Woh kuch begarar logon ko bhi rok lega, jo qabil-e-qabool hai. Aap har bag haath se nahi dhoondte (har mareez ko X-ray) aur scanner chhorte nahi (andaza), aap scanner istemal karte hain.

steps.title: Ottawa ankle rules
steps.detail: Ankle X-ray if there is pain near the ankle and bone tenderness at the back edge or tip of either malleolus, or the patient cannot take four steps (both at the time and in the clinic). For the foot: tenderness at the base of the fifth metatarsal or the navicular. || Ottawa ankle rules

steps.title: Ottawa knee rule
steps.detail: Knee X-ray after an acute injury if any of these is present: age 55 or more; isolated tenderness of the patella; tenderness at the head of the fibula; inability to bend the knee to 90 degrees; inability to take four steps. || Ottawa knee rule

steps.title: Canadian C-spine rule
steps.detail: For alert, stable trauma patients: image if there is a high-risk factor (age 65 or more, a dangerous mechanism, or numbness and tingling in the arms or legs); if not, check low-risk factors that allow safe testing of movement; then image anyone who cannot actively turn the neck 45 degrees to each side. || Canadian C-spine rule

steps.title: Back pain: image only for red flags
steps.detail: Image or refer urgently for suspected cancer or infection (cancer history, weight loss, fever), significant trauma, progressive weakness, signs of cord or cauda equina compression, or a possible fracture in an older or osteoporotic patient. Otherwise treat without a scan. || Kamar dard: sirf red flags par imaging

question.en: A patient with an ankle sprain can take four steps and has no bone tenderness at the malleoli. What do the Ottawa rules say?
question.ur: Ankle sprain wala mareez chaar qadam le sakta hai aur malleoli par haddi ki tenderness nahi. Ottawa rules kya kehte hain?

feedback.en: Yes — the rule is very sensitive, so a negative result makes a fracture very unlikely.
feedback.ur: Haan — rule bohat sensitive hai, is liye negative nateeja fracture ko bohat kam mumkin banata hai.

feedback.en: MRI is not the first step.
That is what the rule avoids.

title.ur: Kamar dard: kis ko imaging chahiye?

rows.en: Mechanical pain, better with movement, no red flags
rows.ur: Mechanical dard, harkat se behtar, red flags nahi

rows.en: Cancer history, weight loss, fever, trauma, night pain, progressive weakness
rows.ur: Cancer ki history, wazan ka girna, bukhar, trauma, raat ka dard, barhti kamzori

rows.en: Normal neurology; leg pain without weakness is not itself a red flag
rows.ur: Normal neurology; kamzori ke baghair taang ka dard khud red flag nahi

rows.en: Saddle numbness, bladder or bowel change, leg weakness, positive cord signs
rows.ur: Saddle sunn hona, peshab ya pakhane mein tabdeeli, taang ki kamzori, cord signs positive

rows.en: Common age-related changes that do not guide treatment
rows.ur: Umar se jure aam tabdeeliyan jo ilaj ki rehnumai nahi karti

rows.en: May change the diagnosis and urgency
rows.ur: Tashkhees aur urgency badal sakta hai

rows.en: Urgent referral, scan as directed by the doctor
rows.ur: Foran referral, scan doctor ki hidayat par

text.en: **Rules for fractures, flags for the spine.** Use Ottawa and the C-spine rule for acute injury, and use red flags (not the length of the pain) to decide on spinal imaging. If a rule says image, refer; if it says not, explain why and reassure.
text.ur: **Fractures ke liye rules, reedh ke liye flags.** Acute chot ke liye Ottawa aur C-spine rule, aur reedh ki imaging ka faisla red flags (dard ki muddat nahi) se karein. Rule kahe imaging to refer karein; na kahe to wajah samjhayein aur tasalli dein.

text.en: **Ordering a scan to reassure.** A scan that shows common changes can make patients more anxious and lead to more treatment and costs without better outcomes. Reassure by explaining the examination and the safe outlook, and keep imaging for the few who need it.
text.ur: **Tasalli ke liye scan karwana.** Aam tabdeeliyan dikhane wala scan mareezon ko zyada pareshan kar sakta hai aur behtar nateejon ke baghair zyada ilaj aur kharch ka sabab banta hai. Examination aur mehfooz nazariye ko samjha kar tasalli dein, aur imaging un chand ke liye rakhein jinhein zaroorat hai.

question.en: A 30-year-old with 2 weeks of back pain, no red flags and a normal neurological exam asks for an MRI. What is the best advice?
question.ur: 30 saal ke mareez ko 2 haftay se kamar dard hai, red flags nahi aur neurological exam normal hai, woh MRI maangta hai. Behtareen mashwara kya hai?

text.en: Tell the patient the pain is imaginary
text.ur: Mareez ko batayein dard khayali hai

feedback.en: The pain is real; the scan is not needed.
feedback.ur: Dard asli hai; scan ki zaroorat nahi.

text.en: Explain that a scan is unlikely to help, treat actively and review in a few weeks
text.ur: Samjhayein ke scan se madad ki umeed kam hai, active ilaj karein aur kuch haftay mein review

feedback.en: Yes — guidelines advise against routine imaging in non-specific back pain.
feedback.ur: Haan — guidelines non-specific kamar dard mein routine imaging ke khilaf mashwara deti hain.

question.en: A 70-year-old falls from a ladder and has neck pain. Under the Canadian C-spine rule, what is the answer?
question.ur: 70 saal ka shakhs seedhi se girta hai aur gardan mein dard hai. Canadian C-spine rule ke mutabiq jawab kya hai?

text.en: Imaging is needed (age 65 or more is a high-risk factor)
text.ur: Imaging chahiye (65 ya zyada umar zyada khatre ka factor hai)

feedback.en: Yes — keep the neck immobilised and refer.
feedback.ur: Haan — gardan ko saakit rakhein aur refer karein.

text.ur: Pehle gardan ki ghumao test karein

feedback.en: Not when a high-risk factor is present.
feedback.ur: Zyada khatre ka factor ho to nahi.

text.ur: Tasalli dein aur halki exercise ka kahein

feedback.ur: Isse fracture miss ho sakta hai.

text.en: **Explain the rule to the patient.** For example: "I have checked the signs that tell us when an X-ray is worth having. None are present, so it is very unlikely you have a fracture, and an X-ray would expose you to radiation without helping. If you cannot put weight on the foot in a few days, or the pain worsens, come back and we will refer you."
text.ur: **Rule mareez ko samjhayein.** Maslan: "Maine woh nishaniyan dekhi hain jo batati hain X-ray kab faida mand hai. Koi maujood nahi, is liye fracture bohat kam mumkin hai, aur X-ray aap ko madad ke baghair radiation dega. Kuch din mein pair par wazan na daal sakein ya dard barhe to wapas aayein aur hum refer karenge."

question.en: Why can a very sensitive rule still send some people without fractures for an X-ray?
question.ur: Bohat sensitive rule phir bhi bina fracture wale kuch logon ko X-ray ke liye kyun bhejti hai?

answer.en: A rule that must almost never miss a fracture sets a low bar for "image", so it also picks up many people without a fracture (low specificity). This trade-off is accepted because missing a fracture is worse than an extra X-ray. The rule's strength is the negative result: it can safely rule out a fracture.
answer.ur: Jo rule fracture lagbhag kabhi miss na kare woh "imaging" ki hadd neechi rakhti hai, is liye woh bina fracture wale bohat se logon ko bhi pakarti hai (kam specificity). Yeh sauda qabool kiya jata hai kyunke fracture miss karna ek ziyada X-ray se bura hai. Rule ki taaqat negative nateeja hai: yeh fracture ko mehfooz taur par rule out kar sakti hai.

beats.patient: A 24-year-old footballer twists his knee, has a swollen joint, tenderness at the head of the fibula, and can walk four steps with a limp but cannot bend the knee past 70 degrees. He is 24.
beats.assessment: Two Ottawa knee criteria are met (tenderness at the head of the fibula and inability to flex to 90 degrees), so an X-ray is indicated to exclude a fracture.
beats.treatment: Protect the knee, avoid loading and refer for an X-ray, and plan further assessment (including ligament tests) after the result.
beats.reassess: The X-ray is normal, so rehabilitation for a ligament sprain starts with the surgeon's agreement.

text.en: **Image or refer urgently** whatever the rule says if there is deformity, severe pain out of proportion, numbness, a pale or cold limb, signs of cord compression, suspected cancer or infection, or a high-energy injury. Decision rules apply to the patients they were built for, usually alert adults; they do not apply to children, confused patients or multiple injuries. Keep the injured area protected until the doctor decides.
text.ur: **Rule kuch bhi kahe, imaging ya foran refer karein** agar bad-shakli, shadeed dard jo chot se mel na khaye, sunn hona, zard ya thanda ang, cord compression ki nishaniyan, cancer ya infection ka shak, ya bari taaqat ki chot ho. Decision rules un mareezon par lagti hain jin ke liye bani, aam taur par hoshiyar bale; yeh bachon, uljhe hue mareezon ya kai chotein wale par nahi lagti. Doctor ke faisle tak chot wale hissay ko mehfooz rakhein.

summary.en: Decision rules (Ottawa ankle and knee, Canadian C-spine) are very sensitive, so a negative result safely avoids an X-ray for the patients they were built for.
summary.ur: Decision rules (Ottawa ankle aur knee, Canadian C-spine) bohat sensitive hain, is liye negative nateeja jin mareezon ke liye bani unke liye X-ray se mehfooz taur par bachata hai.

summary.en: For back pain, image only for red flags or a progressive deficit; most scans show common changes that do not change treatment.
summary.ur: Kamar dard mein sirf red flags ya barhte nuqsan par imaging karein; zyada tar scans aam tabdeeliyan dikhate hain jo ilaj nahi badalti.

summary.en: Explain the rule to the patient, protect the area and refer promptly when a criterion or a red flag is present.
summary.ur: Rule mareez ko samjhayein, hissay ko mehfooz rakhein aur criterion ya red flag ho to jald refer karein.

front.ur: Ottawa knee ke do criteria batayein.

back.en: Age 55 or more, isolated patellar tenderness, fibular head tenderness, cannot flex to 90 degrees, or cannot take four steps.
back.ur: Umar 55 ya zyada, sirf patella ki tenderness, fibula ke sar par tenderness, 90 degree tak flex na kar sakna, ya chaar qadam na le sakna.

front.en: Which patients does the Canadian C-spine rule apply to?
front.ur: Canadian C-spine rule kin mareezon par lagti hai?

front.en: Who needs imaging for back pain?
front.ur: Kamar dard mein kis ko imaging chahiye?

back.en: Those with red flags or a progressive neurological deficit.
back.ur: Jinhein red flags ya barhta neurological nuqsan ho.

front.en: Why is a negative rule result useful?
front.ur: Negative rule nateeja mufeed kyun hai?

back.en: The rule is sensitive, so it can safely rule out a fracture.
back.ur: Rule sensitive hai, is liye fracture ko mehfooz taur par rule out kar sakti hai.
